newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran maquiladora exporters draw up labor code.
newsitem.headline: Honduran maquiladora exporters draw up labor code.

text.p: Exporting manufacturers in Honduras have drawn up a code of conduct and pledged to respect labor laws, an industry leader said Monday.

"The code regulates all matters relating to work by minors, pregnant women, rest days, wages, respect for the environment and human rights," Arnaldo Solis, president of the Honduran Maquiladoras Association, told reporters.

Maquiladoras are manufacturing plants where imported components are assembled for export to take advantage of local conditions such as low wages and tax breaks. Most exports from maquiladora plants in Honduras go to the United States.
"This comes as a recognition by maquiladora firms that laws do exist which govern relations between workers and employers," Solis added.

The Honduran maquiladora industry has recently come under attack for mistreating workers and violating labor laws. Local union leaders say maquiladora workers in Honduras earn an average of 38 cents per hour, the lowest rate in Central America and the Caribbean.
The industry employs a total of 75,000 workers and exported $1.3 billion of goods last year.
